name: HZ_PARTY_PREFERENCES
description: The HZ_PARTY_PREFERENCES table stores information about the preference values provided by a party. Each row defines the preference and the party's specific values for that preference. The preference is the combination of a CATEGORY and a PREFERENCE_CODE. The data type of the preference value can be a string, a number, or a date. The data type determines which VALUE column stores the party's preference value. Oracle Applications use this information to provide personalized information about a party. For example, a record could store the information that the Vision Corporation (PARTY_ID) prefers that their transaction (CATEGORY) currency (PREFERENCE_CODE) is US dollars (VARCHAR2).  . The primary key for this table is PARTY_PREFERENCE_ID.  . The HZ_PARTY_PREFERENCES table stores information about how a party prefers to interact with the system. Please do not attempt to use this table to store extensible attributes of a party.

columns.name: PARTY_PREFERENCE_ID
columns.description: Unique indentifier for the party's preference

columns.name: PARTY_ID
columns.description: Party identifier

columns.name: MODULE
columns.description: The program that creates the preference. For example, TCA MOBILE CUSTOMER DIRECTORY

columns.name: CATEGORY
columns.description: A preference's category can be used to logically group one or more preference codes in a particular user interface. The  combination of CATEGORY and PREFERENCE_CODE identifies a preference.

columns.name: PREFERENCE_CODE
columns.description: A preference code determines if a preference is a single value or a multiple value preference. The preference code is validated by the HZ_PREFERENCE lookup. The combination of CATEGORY and PREFERENCE_CODE identifies a preference.

columns.name: VALUE_VARCHAR2
columns.description: The preference value if the data type is VARCHAR2

columns.name: VALUE_NUMBER
columns.description: The preference value if the data type is NUMBER

columns.name: VALUE_DATE
columns.description: The preference value if the data type is DATE

columns.name: VALUE_NAME
columns.description: A user-defined alias for a preference value

columns.name: ADDITIONAL_VALUE1
columns.description: Additional preference value

columns.name: ADDITIONAL_VALUE2
columns.description: Additional preference value

columns.name: ADDITIONAL_VALUE3
columns.description: Additional preference value

columns.name: ADDITIONAL_VALUE4
columns.description: Additional preference value

columns.name: ADDITIONAL_VALUE5
columns.description: Additional preference value

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.description: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: CONFLICT_ID
columns.description: Disconnected Mobile: this value is used to guarantee the uniqueness of the row when duplicates are created in different databases (i.e. mobile databases or the server).

columns.name: USER_LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Disconnected Mobile: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row. This value is different from LAST_UPDATE_DATE if the update originally happened in a different database (i.e. a different mobile database or the server).

columns.name: CPDRF_VER_SOR
columns.description: Cross Pillar Data Replication Framework (CPDRF) system column for tracking record version in System of Record (SOR) pillar when a  record change is replicated to subscribing pillars by the replication flows.

columns.name: CPDRF_VER_PILLAR
columns.description: Cross Pillar Data Replication Framework (CPDRF) system column for tracking record version when a record is changed by replication flows

columns.name: CPDRF_LAST_UPD
columns.description: Cross Pillar Data Replication Framework (CPDRF) system column for tracking source pillar name when a record is changed by the replication flows.

columns.name: STATUS_FLAG
columns.description: Record Status Flag used to soft delete entity. Possible values are 'A' (active) and 'I' (inactive).
